summary_1line: Sauti explains the origin of Samanta‑panchaka, the scale of an Akshauhini army, and outlines the many parvas composing the Mahabharata.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama Parashurama stands amid five newly formed lakes of blood after destroying the Kshatriyas, offering oblations to his ancestors.
Eighteen vast Akshauhini armies of chariots, elephants, cavalry, and infantry assemble across the open plain of Samanta‑panchaka before the great war.
Bhima and Duryodhana clash with heavy maces in a final duel at dusk on the battlefield after the armies have been destroyed.
